links.outcome: Hallucination rate and coding accuracy of LLM-generated OPS codes from surgical reports
links.effect: GPT CodeMedic showed fewer hallucinations than GPT-4o (7% vs. 15%); sufficient coding accuracy GPT-4o 78%, GPT CodeMedic 89% vs coders 100%.
links.quote: The specialized GPT CodeMedic tends to show fewer hallucinations compared to GPT-4o (7% vs. 15%).

links.outcome: Comparing LLM coding against surgeons and professional coders on same reports
links.effect: Coders (100%) and surgeons (99%) outperformed LLMs in sufficient coding (GPT-4o 78%, GPT CodeMedic 89%; p<0.01); for optimal coding GPT CodeMedic (83%) outperformed surgeons (69%, p=0.03).
links.quote: Currently, professional coders still significantly outperform LLMs in sufficient and optimal coding.

unlisted_practices: Using LLMs to automate billing/procedure code extraction from operative reports
Using a domain-specialized custom GPT versus general LLM to reduce errors

screen.reason: Empirical retrospective evaluation comparing LLM performance (GPT-4o and GPT CodeMedic) to surgeons and professional coders for extracting billing/procedure (OPS) codes from operative reports.
